svg.title: How Minimum Net Charges Erode Headline Discounts
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-minimum-charge-discount-erosion; chapter number: 3; title: How Minimum Net Charges Erode Headline Discounts; subtitle: Two worked carrier-contract examples, in discount percentage points; chart type: waterfall; bars: label: Shipware Headline Discount; value: 50; display: 50% off; kind: total; label: $8.23 Minimum Net Charge Pin; value: -12; display: -12 pts; kind: deduction; label: Shipware Effective Discount; value: 38; display: 38% effective; kind: result; label: LJM Grid Plus Tier Headline; value: 35; display: 35% (23% grid + 12% tier); kind: total; label: LJM Minimum Floor Constraint; value: -13; display: -13 pts; kind: deduction; label: LJM Constrained Discount; value: 22; display: ~22% effective; kind: result; caption: Keith Myers works a Zone 4, 10 lb package at $13.27: 50% off nets $6.64, but the $8.23 minimum makes the effective discount 38%, and a 65% offer would save nothing. LJM shows a stacked 23% grid plus 12% tier constrained to about 22%, and tells shippers to maximize the grid portion.; assumptions note: Deduction bars are the point gap between each reported headline and effective discount. Scarbrough Global reports 25-35% from full contract engineering versus about 3% (range 1-5%) from audit alone, over 3-6 negotiation rounds across 6-10 weeks per LJM.; note: Attributed to Shipware (rjelY0C_iQg), LJM (56winzXYmPA), Scarbrough Global (jEjymzbOEFQ), and Refund Retriever (JAnVvaSg0TA), which calls the minimum net charge a basement floor under discounts.
